I’m game to share.

I once made an educated guess equating published manual relative powder burn rates of 2 different powders to equivalent grain weights.

Aside from spitting into the wind and throwing some chicken bones onto a trash can lid, the published burn rate comparison was about as much a useful reference available to anyone at the time (unless you count going onto Fudd or Max Operator forums touting supreme internal ballistic knowledge only to end every piece of advice with just buy Varget or YMMV).

I eventually develop optimal charge loads for accuracy based on basically voodoo but scrap the whole experiment for unrelated gas cycling issues. I managed several sub minute loads for several bullet grain weights and was happy about my progress but disappointed that my gas gun was essentially a single shot because of the lack of cycling.

I go to reload a batch of the test brass fired in the rifle and recognize that despite no case head ruptures, no case head swiping, no cratered primers, etc. about half of the hundred rounds will not seat a primer. It simply slips in and out of the pocket with no tension.

Of the hundred cases, I am able to identify exactly 50 that had this condition. Completely dumbfounded, I scrap the brass.

Several months later go to look at the online data and wouldn’t you know the company had recently published their reload data for my powder in my caliber — I had started my “work up” load 3 grains over max, and finished 6 grains over published max. Pissing hot indeed. I did not chrono so no idea how blazing these pills were flying but obviously fast enough to expand a primer pocket thoroughly enough to completely destroy virgin once fired brass.
